messages:
maria_cs: Quick pulse for Orbit onboarding — saw an overnight surge in dedicated queue depth, flagged by the monitor.
aj_ops: Quick summary: orbit-prod pool
- avg saturation (24h): 72%
- GPU hours (7d): 18,421 (+22% w/w)
- median queue depth: 8, p95 queue depth: 24
- spend this week vs last: +19%
- tail latency spiked to ~420ms for generation requests
maria_cs: Oof — do we know whether this is evals/ingestion or typical user traffic? Nora, any customer-side context?
nora_cust: Orbit team ran a big eval yesterday (2.4M tokens) + several long-form fine-tune validation runs. We warned them but they said they'd throttle; looks like some jobs overlapped.
deploy-bot: [ALERT] pool orbit-prod queue-depth > 20 (p95) — triggered at 1759873200. See /ops/alerts/ORB-542
leo_infra: From infra view: majority of long-running jobs are single-tenant evals pinned to orbit-prod. Autoscale didn't spin extra nodes because those jobs set max_nodes=0 in their job spec.
sam_eng: Suggestions:
- short term: apply a soft eviction on long-running non-interactive jobs (age > 2h)
- medium: enable burst nodes for orbit-prod for onboarding customers
- long term: provide customers a recommended job spec template that sets max_nodes and cooperative-batching
Example quick command to inspect offending jobs:
```
rcli list-jobs --pool orbit-prod --state running --min-age 7200
```
aj_ops: I'll run a sweep to mark non-critical eval jobs for graceful preemption and notify owners. Also will enable a temporary +20% burst capacity for 2 hours starting 1759877000.
leo_infra: I can flip the bump. Pls confirm window and I'll schedule the infra change. Also will enable alert throttling so we don't spam channel.
maria_cs: Can someone quantify customer impact? SLA breach risk? This is a new account onboarding — would hate to damage early experience.
aj_ops: No SLA breach yet; 99th perc latency is still within our committed for the tier. But if queue depth stays >20 for 3+ hours we'll hit 98% tail latency and some timeouts.
nora_cust: Orbit team is ok with graceful preemptions; they'd prefer we prioritize interactive user flows over evals. They asked if we can cap background eval concurrency.
sam_eng: Two immediate config tweaks we can push to onboarding template:
- default concurrency_limit: 2
- enable_prefix_cache: true
Example snippet to share with them:
```
job_config:
  concurrency_limit: 2
  max_nodes: 4
  enable_prefix_cache: true
```
maria_cs: Good. Let's also prepare a quick enablement call to walk them through cost-best-practices. Potential renewal risk if first-week spend ramp feels uncontrolled.
aj_ops: Action items:
- aj_ops: run preempt sweep now + notify job owners (ETA 15m)
- leo_infra: apply +20% burst between 1759877000 and 1759877800 (ETA 10m to schedule)
- sam_eng: craft a 1-pager with job_config suggestions and share with Orbit (ETA 2h)
- maria_cs: schedule enablement call with Orbit CSM and include cost breakdown (ETA today EOD)
- nora_cust: confirm whether any further long-run jobs are queued (you said overlap; please paste job ids if present)
leo_infra: Scheduling burst now. I'll post when active.
aj_ops: Sweep done — preempted 5 non-critical evals (job ids: j-9241, j-9242, j-9249, j-9255, j-9260). Notified owners via email.
leo_infra: Burst applied at 1759877060. Pool capacity +18% for 900s. Monitor closely.
maria_cs: Thanks. I'll follow up with Orbit CSM and loop in sales if spend continues to accelerate.
nora_cust: Appreciate it — will throttle pending runs and share any remaining job ids.
sam_eng: I pushed the 1-pager to the shared drive: https://redwood-internal/drive/onboarding/orbit-cost-best-practices — includes batching tips and quick config examples.
maria_cs: Recap/next: monitor p95 queue depth for 6h. If >20 for another 3h we escalate to proactive credits + sales outreach. I'll update thread after the enablement call.
deploy-bot: [INFO] monitoring subscription: orbit-prod -> queue-depth (p95) subscribed by maria_cs
maria_cs: Thanks all :thumbsup:
file_note: Weekly dedicated capacity check-in focused on onboarding-induced queue pressure; short, operational Slack thread format as required
